A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BOOM and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be reliably matched, including the removal of Appendix C.3 from v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original BOOM evaluations on 14 locomotion tasks, component ablations, and a Gaussian-mixture fitting experiment, alongside some reused baseline results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original BOOM benchmark results, component ablations, and Gaussian-mixture fitting experiment.

M1.justification: The published loss specification changes: Equation 4 adds a horizon sum, and Equation 5 places both Q and the alignment term inside the negatively signed sum. Algorithm 1 also changes the replay horizon endpoint from H to H−1. The architecture and bootstrap procedure remain; the new alignment sign conflicts with the retained explanation, so an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven DMC tasks, seven Humanoid-Bench tasks, and Gaussian-mixture fitting problem. Appendix B.1 retains the same task requirements and environments. Revised training budgets do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain SAC, DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, and BMPC. However, removing Appendix C.3/Figure 15 eliminates the supplementary 10M-step SAC comparison, while longer-budget DreamerV3 entries remain in Table 1. The newly discussed TDM(PC)2 is not evaluated.

E3.justification: DreamerV3 budgets change from 4M/10M environment steps to 2M/10M iterations; BMPC budget matching is likewise described in iterations. Table 2 changes warmup from 1,000 to 5,000 steps, and Section 4.3 changes the Humanoid-Bench alignment coefficient from dim(A)/100 to dim(A)/50. These are reported setting revisions; reruns and conversion to the unchanged environment-step axes are not established.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3/Figure 15 is removed, losing the supplementary examination of whether longer training improves the initially weak SAC and DreamerV3 baselines. The three Dog-run component/sensitivity ablations, Gaussian-mixture illustration, and locomotion visualizations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds, report mean ± standard deviation in Table 1, and describe Figure 2 shading as confidence intervals over three runs. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure, run count, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: All 96 mean/standard-deviation entries in Table 1 are unchanged, including BOOM averages of 877.7 on DMC and 820.6 on Humanoid-Bench. The retained benchmark and ablation curves also match. Figure 15's extended SAC/DreamerV3 trajectories and accompanying findings are removed, although DreamerV3's longer-budget table values remain. Revised budget labels do not demonstrate a performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equations 4–5 revise the mathematical loss definitions through temporal summation and changed grouping. In particular, Equation 5's new brackets change the alignment term's sign rather than merely its typography. Theorems 1–2 and all lemmas, assumptions, and proofs in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: bootstrap policy–planner alignment, a likelihood-free forward-KL objective, soft Q-weighting, and superior stability and performance on high-dimensional control tasks. The central claims are neither narrowed nor expanded.

C2.justification: The explanations of actor divergence, improved world-model learning, forward-KL behavior, and Q-weighting remain. Appendix D retains the same planning-overhead and model-error limitations and future directions. The removed longer-budget observations do not introduce a different interpretation of the retained findings.

D1.justification: The stated humanoid action dimension changes from 24 to 21, hyperparameter values are revised, and the approximately 50-hour Dog-run training time is now associated with 2M iterations rather than 4M environment steps. Hardware, architecture, and code-access information remain. Removing the duplicate 1% value-dropout entry does not remove the retained equivalent 0.01 Q-function dropout disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds an explicit discussion of concurrent TDM(PC)2, distinguishing its stated TD3+BC/reverse-KL approach from BOOM's AWAC-like critic weighting and forward KL. That work was already cited as reference 25 in v1; the bibliography itself is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and notation edits, expands affiliations, changes corresponding-author marking and acknowledgments, adds the concurrent-work paragraph, and removes Appendix C.3 and its cross-reference. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 15's extended-budget curve grid is removed. Table 1 receives a revised budget heading, Table 2 reorganizes its warmup/dropout entries, and nearby text and figures reflow. The other scientific figures retain their content without a broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The explicit positioning against TDM(PC)2 is useful, but v3 introduces a sign inconsistency in Equation 5: its new brackets negate the alignment loss despite the retained instruction to minimize it. Removing Appendix C.3/Figure 15 also reduces evidence about longer-budget baseline convergence while preserving the broad performance claims. These limited losses in mathematical clarity and experimental transparency outweigh the localized clarifications.
